extra.message: Hardcoded default session/HMAC secret key — Attacker who knows the default can forge valid session cookies (impersonate any user including admin) and forge API-key/reset-token hashes. [verified: app/config.py:13 falls back to the publicly-known literal 'dev-only-change-me-support-desk', and security.py uses settings.secret_key to sign session cookies (URLSafeTimedSerializer) and HMAC reset/API-key tokens with no startup check rejecting the default, so an unset SECRET_KEY lets an attacker forge admin sessions and token hashes.]

Cross-org ticket creation / user provisioning via integration API key — Any valid API key can create tickets and provision customer accounts in arbitrary organizations, crossing tenant isolation. [verified: ApiKey model has no organization/tenant field, and create_ticket_from_api resolves the org solely from attacker-controlled payload.organization_external_ref with no key-to-tenant binding, so any valid API key can create tickets and auto-provision customer_user accounts (emailing temp passwords) in arbitrary organizations, breaking per-org isolation.]

Integration API ticket status update lacks tenant scoping (cross-org BOLA) — Any valid integration API key can transition the status of arbitrary tickets belonging to other organizations, corrupting workflow state and triggering webhooks for tickets they should not control. [verified: Same code path: db.get(Ticket, ticket_id) at app/routers/integrations.py:76 plus transition_ticket performs no tenant scoping, and ApiKey lacks any organization_id, so any X-API-Key holder can transition arbitrary tickets across organizations by iterating ticket_id, also triggering ticket.updated webhooks.]

CSV formula injection in admin report export — Spreadsheet formula injection/command execution for staff opening admin report CSVs. [verified: export_report builds CSV rows from attacker-controlled ticket subject (free-text str, schemas.py:122), organization name, and requester email, then passes them to csv_response (services.py:292) which uses a bare csv.DictWriter with no neutralization of cells starting with = + - @. Staff opening the report CSV are exposed to spreadsheet formula injection.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag by default — Session token can be sniffed over HTTP, enabling session hijacking. [verified: config.py defaults secure_cookies to false and set_session_cookie uses secure=settings.secure_cookies, so the HttpOnly session cookie is sent over plain HTTP by default, exposing it to interception.]

Missing brute-force protection on authentication endpoints — Attackers can brute-force passwords and reset tokens at unlimited speed. [verified: login, request_reset, and confirm_reset perform credential/token checks with no throttling; a codebase-wide search for rate limiting returns no matches in deps.py or main.py, leaving brute-force unprotected.]

Password reset token written to plaintext outbox log — Anyone with file/log access can read reset tokens and take over accounts. [verified: request_reset (auth.py:110) passes the plaintext reset token into send_mock_email, which writes the full body to settings.email_outbox on disk as plaintext JSON (services.py:124-128); the DB only stores the hash, so the usable secret persists in cleartext on disk readable by anyone with file/log access. Reachable via unauthenticated /api/auth/password-reset/request, but exploitation requires local]

CSV formula injection in reports export — Spreadsheet formula injection / command execution for users opening exported report CSVs. [verified: export_report builds CSV rows from attacker-controlled fields (organization.name set from unauthenticated registration payload.organization_name, ticket subject from payload.subject) and passes them to csv_response, which uses plain csv.DictWriter with no prefixing/escaping of leading formula characters (=,+,-,@), confirming CSV formula injection.]

CSV formula injection in scoped ticket export — Formula/command execution in the spreadsheet of whoever opens the exported CSV, enabling data exfiltration or code execution. [verified: `export_scoped_tickets` (tickets.py:91) writes attacker-controlled ticket `subject`, `organization.name`, and `requester.email` into CSV via `csv_response`/`csv.DictWriter` (services.py:292), which performs no neutralization of leading `= + - @`; the schema only enforces length, so a customer-supplied formula like `=cmd|'/c calc'!A1` reaches staff spreadsheets verbatim.]

CSV formula injection in ticket/report exports — When a staff user opens an exported CSV in a spreadsheet, attacker-crafted ticket subjects can execute formulas (data exfiltration, command execution via DDE). [verified: Same csv_response sink writes untrusted subject/organization/email fields without sanitizing formula-trigger characters; /api/tickets/export.csv and reports exports include customer/integration-sourced subjects, so a crafted subject executes as a formula on open.]

CSV formula injection in ticket/report exports — Spreadsheet formula execution / data exfiltration on the machine of staff who open exported CSVs. [verified: csv_response (app/services.py) uses csv.DictWriter with no neutralization of leading =,+,-,@; tickets.py:101 and reports/admin exports feed attacker-controlled ticket subject, organization.name, and requester.email into cells, enabling spreadsheet formula injection when staff open the CSV.]

Account/organization enumeration on registration — Attacker can determine valid registered emails and existing organizations, aiding targeted attacks. [verified: register raises 409 'Email is already registered' vs 409 'Organization already exists' (auth.py:62-64), distinct from login's generic 401 'Invalid credentials', allowing enumeration of valid emails and organizations.]

Unvalidated escalation owner assignment (mass assignment) — A staff user can set an escalation owner to an arbitrary user id (including out-of-team/non-staff), bypassing the ownership validation enforced elsewhere. [verified: request_escalation in tickets.py sets owner_id=payload.owner_id directly from EscalationCreate with no existence/role/team validation, whereas update_escalation validates owner.role in {team_lead,support_admin} and team scope; a staff user can assign an arbitrary/out-of-scope/non-staff owner_id. Impact is limited to the escalation owner field and requires authenticated staff, with no direct access]
